articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Jerry, the king of dogs, who taught me how to live
articles.summary: After a burglary, my parents decided we needed extra security. Jerry was the answer – and this hungry, handsome hound helped us all in countless ways. Jerry came into our lives because a burglar had broken in. My mum had woken in the middle of the night to find an intruder in our kitchen.
body: Jerry was very laid-back and Zen. He became part of the family straight away. He also became the therapy dog we hadn’t realised we needed. With two teenagers in the house (me and my older brother) and a hyperactive younger brother, someone was always in a strop and needing to let off steam by taking him out for a walk. Each time, Jerry obliged. I’d bore him with my latest teen-romance trauma; he was a very good listener. Sometimes, he’d have five walks a day, with both of my parents taking their turn. He certainly got his steps in.

He also dined in style. Most dogs loiter under the table during meal times. Jerry would climb on top of it and make himself comfortable until dinner was served. Often, I would come home from school and catch him lying there regally, waiting for his next banquet. It wasn’t scraps that interested him; he wanted the full three courses. He particularly liked deli food – salt beef, potato salad, pastrami, coleslaw, even apple strudel. One day, a big bowl of chopped liver disappeared. My mum blamed me, my brothers, then my dad, before realising who the culprit was.
points: After a burglary, my parents decided we needed extra security.
Jerry was the answer – and this hungry, handsome hound helped us all in countless ways.

articles.title: Do you have a bespoke ‘dirty zone’? | Emma Beddington
articles.summary: Apparently a dedicated mud room will make you less stressed. But I have a very different approach. I was excited to learn that the latest interiors essential, according to the Washington Post, is a “dirty zone”.
body: Does this make me kinda chic? Unfortunately not: the Post is actually preaching the benefits of confining the sordid ephemera of life to carefully delineated and hidden areas: storage benches, monogrammed totes or even a “mud room” (for coats, shoes, skis, lacrosse sticks and dog-washing sinks – I think posh Britons call it a boot room). A 2021 study in the Netherlands found that participants who did chores in chaotic environments had higher levels of the stress marker salivary alpha-amylase. I always wonder what’s brewing in my mouth as I fall over piles of filthy shoes yet again while running to answer the door.

This dirty zone system sounds nice, but deeply, decadently unrealistic. A mud room, rather than various rooms containing some mud, surely isn’t something most people have. If you do, apparently you’ll also want a $115 (£85) petitgrain and neroli reed diffuser, to help mask the smell. One expert consulted by the Post suggested green as a mud room colour scheme, to coordinate harmoniously with your brown delivery boxes “if you’re a heavy Amazon shopper”, which has a real last-days-of-Rome ring to it.

articles.title: The one change that worked: I stopped listening to podcasts – and my mind flooded with ideas
articles.summary: For decades my life was soundtracked by comedy duos, mostly male, discussing their friendships. When I gave them up, I felt as if I was having a mental reboot. I have always loved podcasts.
body: I have always loved podcasts. The genre of audio I have come to think of as Two Men Talking (In Excessive Detail About Their Lives) has been one of my favourite forms of entertainment for decades. It started with a semi-religious devotion to a Sunday morning XFM show hosted by Jimmy Carr and the comedy writer Iain Morris, but as the years progressed and podcasting boomed, I was soon spoilt for choice. Eventually there were enough comedy duos candidly discussing their hopes, fears and awkward social interactions to fill every moment of my day.

I was initially drawn to these podcasts because they made me laugh, but from the start I also found them hugely comforting: there was a period in my teenage years when I couldn’t fall asleep without mainlining episodes of Adam and Joe’s BBC 6 Music show, waking up each morning relieved I hadn’t been strangled by my iPod earphones in the night.

When I gave them up, I felt as if I was having a mental reboot.

articles.title: Is it true that … mental health is affected by inflammation?
articles.summary: Studies have found that anti-inflammatory drugs can improve your mood. But what does that mean for conditions such as depression and anxiety? Inflammation is the immune system’s response to injury or infection.
body: But inflammation can also occur in the body during illnesses, and a low level of inflammation can arise from obesity or ageing. “A marker of that inflammation tends to be elevated cytokines in people’s blood,” says Prof Daniel M Davis, head of life sciences at Imperial College London and author of Immune Health: A Myth-Busting Guide. “They’re the molecules immune cells use to communicate with each other.”

There are more than 100 types of cytokines in your body, and some affect the brain. “If you have a fever, it’s not just physical, you’re also mentally affected,” says Davis. “Some cytokines influence how you feel.”

Studies of patients with rheumatoid arthritis have found that cytokine-blocking anti-inflammatory drugs can also improve mood. Scans suggest this may be because blocking cytokines changes activity in the brain.

articles.title: Fall and Suede Bags Were Made for Each Other
articles.summary: Shop the season’s must-have suede bags, from structured top-handles to roomy, relaxed shapes—perfect for adding a touch of texture to your wardrobe.
body: Suede, suede, suede! While not new to fashion, we can only describe the material’s resurgence as impressive—and lasting. Brands have taken note and are utilizing the luxe, soft handle for jackets, belts, kitten heels, and notably, handbags. The new crop of suede handbags on the market proves just how sophisticated, modern, and unique they can be.

What’s additionally exciting is that, at the moment, designers are playing with a range of silhouettes that show off suede’s versatility. There are slouchy, relaxed shapes from Khaite and Balenciaga—styles that pair easily with leather midiskirts and sporty outerwear. In that vein, Gucci’s reimaging the hobo bag, amplifying the bohemian nature of suede—in tones that range from chocolate brown and sandy beige. Likewise, polished shapes are trending, with structured top-handles from Burberry, Nili Lotan, and Bottega Veneta being the perfect counterpoint to more ladylike looks.

There are investment styles that will stand the test of time, and more affordable options to experiment with the trend before plunging into the deep end. Ahead, a range of the best suede bags to add to your fall rotation.
points: Shop the season’s must-have suede bags, from structured top-handles to roomy, relaxed shapes—perfect for adding a touch of texture to your wardrobe.

articles.title: When a Friend Steals Your Baby Name
articles.summary: “It was a family name that my entire girl group knew about, so when this particular friend announced she was going to use it, we were all shocked—especially because I was single at the time.”
body: Betrayal comes in many forms. But when it comes to crimes against the sisterhood, there are only a few unforgivable sins; acts that rupture friendship groups, end decades-long relationships, and make you question everything you thought you knew. People might get over a friend hooking up with someone they liked in college. There will always be gossip. And spilling a secret you swore you’d keep—at least once—is practically par for the course. But nobody gets over it when someone steals your baby name.

We can all remember that Sex and the City episode. The one where Charlotte discovers her old friend Laney will be calling her daughter “Shayla,” a name Charlotte claimed to have invented when she was 11 and told all of her friends about, making them promise not to use it. Former party girl Laney denies culpability and rolls her eyes: “I can’t believe you’re freaking out over a name.” Another friend concurs, “You’re not even pregnant.”

This is all happening at Laney’s baby shower, by the way. Samantha arrives and asks what’s going on. After Charlotte explains, the ardently loyal Samantha simply turns to Laney and says, “You bitch!” It’s one of the most quoted moments in the series.

articles.title: 22 Easy Weeknight Dinners for September
articles.summary: Curry-glazed salmon, crispy gnocchi caprese, and more more easy dinners for busy nights.
body: September is a sweet spot for easy weeknight cooking: a little bit summer, a little bit fall, it’s raw produce’s time to shine. Tomatoes, peppers, and basil are coming in strong, and there’s so much zucchini, farmers are practically giving it away. At the same time, the first signs of fall (apples! turning leaves! your coffee shop’s seasonal menu!) are popping up left, right, and center.

All the while, schedules are filling up. Between back-to-school, soccer practice, the end of summer Fridays, and the post-Labor Day blues, your nightly meal plan should be a beacon. That means make-ahead recipes you can prep before the evening rush, one-pot dinners that save you from a sink full of dishes, and 30-minute meals for nights when hunger overcometh you. There are dinners that rely on summer’s last tomatoes, a marinated lentil salad that’s even better by lunchtime the next day, and a couple of cozy soups because blustery days are right around the corner.
points: Curry-glazed salmon, crispy gnocchi caprese, and more more easy dinners for busy nights.

articles.title: 10 Black-and-White Outfits to Master Transitional Dressing
articles.summary: From white tees and fluid black trousers to sleek skirts and lightweight layers, here are 10 black and white outfits to try—with styling tricks to elevate each.
body: There’s no denying that the fall 2026 runways made a strong case for color; even the street style scene is on board, slipping into colorful shoes and sporting handbags in a variety of vibrant shades—baby pink, chartreuse, and cobalt. Still, there’s something about going back to basics at the dawn of a new season that feels especially right. Enter the tried-and-true minimalist uniform: the black-and-white outfit.

A longtime fashion-girl favorite, the look is clean, refined, and, perhaps best of all, leaves ample room for playful styling tricks—think tassel scarves worn as cumberbunds, lace sarongs, and even fringe belts. During Copenhagen Fashion Week, the monochrome palette appeared on nearly every showgoer—a stark contrast to the week’s historically maximalist approach. One look in particular was on our radar: a long-sleeve white tee with a simple black satin slip skirt, finished with a pair of elegant velvet slippers. The result was casual, comfortable, and entirely cool.
points: From white tees and fluid black trousers to sleek skirts and lightweight layers, here are 10 black and white outfits to try—with styling tricks to elevate each.

articles.title: This Stylish New Scottish Highlands Retreat Is a Love Letter to Its Natural Surroundings
articles.summary: As Europe’s largest private conservation project, WildLand is as much about impeccable design as it is about protecting the local flora and fauna.
body: Except, of course, that wasn’t entirely true; already, by then, Scotland’s fragile landscape was under threat from ecological degradation. Nearly a century on, it ranks among the most nature-depleted countries in the world, with land mismanagement across grouse moors and deer parks a contributing factor. As one laird I speak to puts it: “That Romantic vision that everyone has from Landseer paintings—the endless heaths, the rolling glens—really, that’s a biodiversity disaster captured in real time.”

It’s a crisis WildLand is hoping to remedy with a 200-year vision. Established in 2006 by Danish businessman Anders Holch Povlsen—the largest private landowner in Scotland—the conservation group’s holdings now encompass more than 222,000 acres, with a hospitality arm that immerses guests in rewilded landscapes. (More than six million trees have been hand-planted by Wildland in the last 12 years alone.) Aldourie Castle, a turreted pile on the shores of Loch Ness, and Killiehuntly Farmhouse, a slate-roofed retreat nestled in the granite peaks of the Cairngorms, are among its flagship properties—but its latest opening on the northwest coast might pip them both to become the standout.
points: As Europe’s largest private conservation project, WildLand is as much about impeccable design as it is about protecting the local flora and fauna.
